We provide a partially functorial and constructive reconstruction procedure for formal schemes from symmetric monoidal categories of nuclear modules. More precisely, for a formal scheme $\mathfrak{X}$, we show that the torsion subcategory $D_{\mathrm{tors}}(\mathfrak{X})$ can be recovered as the maximal strongly compactly generated localizing tensor ideal of Efimov's category $\mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{Ef}}(\mathfrak{X})$, and similarly for the Clausen--Scholze category $\mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{CS}}(\mathfrak{X})$. Combining this with the Balmer spectrum, we reconstruct $\mathfrak{X}$ from the corresponding symmetric monoidal category of nuclear modules. Moreover, for formal schemes topologically of finite type over a field or over $\mathbb{Z}$, the contravariant functor $\mathfrak{X} \mapsto \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{Ef}}(\mathfrak{X})$ is fully faithful; in the affine case, the analogous statement holds for $\mathfrak{X} \mapsto \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{CS}}(\mathfrak{X})$.

1 Introduction The aim of this paper is to establish a reconstruction result for formal schemes from Efimov’s and Clausen–Scholze categories of nuclear modules. For a formal scheme 𝔛 \mathfrak{X} , let Nuc Ef ​ ( 𝔛 ) \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{Ef}}(\mathfrak{X}) denote Efimov’s category of nuclear modules [ 8 ] , and let Nuc CS ​ ( 𝔛 ) \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{CS}}(\mathfrak{X}) denote the Clausen–Scholze category of nuclear modules in the sense of [ 13 , 1 , 2 ] . For an ∞ \infty -category C C , we denote its homotopy category by Ho ⁡ ( C ) \mathrm{Ho}(C) . Theorem 1.1 (Corollary 5.2 ) . Let 𝔛 , 𝔜 \mathfrak{X},\mathfrak{Y} be Noetherian formal schemes. (1). If there is a symmetric monoidal triangulated equivalence Ho ⁡ ( Nuc Ef ​ ( 𝔛 ) ) ≅ Ho ⁡ ( Nuc Ef ​ ( 𝔜 ) ) \mathrm{Ho}(\mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{Ef}}(\mathfrak{X}))\cong\mathrm{Ho}(\mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{Ef}}(\mathfrak{Y})) , then 𝔛 ≅ 𝔜 \mathfrak{X}\cong\mathfrak{Y} . (2). If 𝔛 , 𝔜 \mathfrak{X},\mathfrak{Y} are affine, and there is a symmetric monoidal triangulated equivalence Ho ⁡ ( Nuc CS ​ ( 𝔛 ) ) ≅ Ho ⁡ ( Nuc CS ​ ( 𝔜 ) ) \mathrm{Ho}(\mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{CS}}(\mathfrak{X}))\cong\mathrm{Ho}(\mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{CS}}(\mathfrak{Y})) , then 𝔛 ≅ 𝔜 \mathfrak{X}\cong\mathfrak{Y} . Moreover, we give a partially functorial and constructive reconstruction. The proof is roughly as follows. First, we recover the derived category D tors ​ ( 𝔛 ) D_{\mathrm{tors}}(\mathfrak{X}) of torsion modules from the nuclear categories Nuc Ef ​ ( 𝔛 ) \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{Ef}}(\mathfrak{X}) and Nuc CS ​ ( 𝔛 ) \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{CS}}(\mathfrak{X}) . More precisely, D tors ​ ( 𝔛 ) D_{\mathrm{tors}}(\mathfrak{X}) is recovered as a certain maximal strongly compactly generated localizing ideal. Next, we recover the formal scheme 𝔛 \mathfrak{X} itself from D tors ​ ( 𝔛 ) D_{\mathrm{tors}}(\mathfrak{X}) by using a slight modification of Balmer’s tensor triangular spectrum. We also discuss a second reconstruction method in the spirit of Liu’s functorial spectrum [ 9 ] . Instead of first extracting D tors ​ ( 𝔛 ) D_{\mathrm{tors}}(\mathfrak{X}) , this method uses field-valued points of the nuclear category. It yields the following full faithfulness result. We prove this in a more general form in Theorem 6.7 . In Section 2, we introduce notation and recall basic properties of triangulated categories, tensor triangulated categories, and categories associated with formal schemes. In Section 3, we prove that the maximal strongly compactly generated localizing ideals of Nuc Ef ​ ( 𝔛 ) \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{Ef}}(\mathfrak{X}) and Nuc CS ​ ( 𝔛 ) \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{CS}}(\mathfrak{X}) are given by the derived category of torsion modules D tors ​ ( 𝔛 ) D_{\mathrm{tors}}(\mathfrak{X}) . In Section 4, we introduce a modification of Balmer’s tensor triangular spectrum and apply it to D tors ​ ( 𝔛 ) D_{\mathrm{tors}}(\mathfrak{X}) . Since the unit object of D tors ​ ( 𝔛 ) D_{\mathrm{tors}}(\mathfrak{X}) is not compact, we need to slightly modify the usual definition. We also prove the functoriality needed later. In Section 5, we give a partially functorial and constructive reconstruction of formal schemes. In Section 6, we give another approach to reconstruction and, as a consequence, prove the full faithfulness of the functors Nuc Ef \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{Ef}} and Nuc CS \mathrm{Nuc}^{\mathrm{CS}} . Assumptions and Notation We assume the existence of a Grothendieck universe. All rings are assumed to be commutative and unital. All formal schemes are assumed to be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and to admit a finitely generated ideal of definition locally. Unless otherwise specified, all triangulated categories are assumed to admit small coproducts and to be well generated. By an ∞ \infty -category, we mean an ( ∞ , 1 ) (\infty,1) -category. We regard ordinary categories and ( 2 , 1 ) (2,1) -categories as ∞ \infty -categories in the usual way. For a functor F F , we denote its right adjoint, when it exists, by F R F^{\mathrm{R}} .
